about: Closed vocabulary for title registers, the house exhibit digest and the page library's tags: the terms the 578-page coded corpus was tagged in. Each slug names one term; the label is its wording. Two annotation moves are terms the corpus coders used under no row of their own (their labels say so). complete_guide.py and library.py refuse any value outside these lists, so a new term enters here first. annotation_kind_moves maps each annotation kind that can be drawn with no words of its own to the digest moves it draws: a house precedent for an unlabelled mark (annotate.py) is a digest move of that list answered labelled false.

title_companion_above.kicker: Kicker or eyebrow label above the title
title_companion_above.other: Something else; say what in why

title_companion_below.subtitle: Subtitle
title_companion_below.lead_in: Lead-in sentence or claim under a topic title
title_companion_below.other: Something else; say what in why

exhibit_type.line: Line (incl. indexed, price, dual-axis, area to baseline)
exhibit_type.stacked: Stacked bar, column or area (incl. 100%, diverging)

data_shape.no_data_shape: None of the data shapes above (an image wall, big numbers, structured text); say what in why

message_kind.other: None of the message kinds above; the message field says it

annotation_move.highlight_one_mute_rest: Highlight one item, mute the rest
annotation_move.callout_to_insight: Callout box, arrow or leader to the insight
annotation_move.end_or_direct_labels: End or direct labels instead of a legend
annotation_move.numbered_keys: Numbered or lettered keys tied to text
annotation_move.data_rows_under_chart: Data rows or a table aligned under the chart
annotation_move.event_markers: Event markers on a time axis
annotation_move.bracket_or_brace: Bracket or brace (often with a sum)
annotation_move.inset_stats_table: Inset stats table inside the plot
annotation_move.connectors_between_marks: Connectors or zoom lines between marks
annotation_move.statistic_row_emphasis: Median or statistic row or block emphasised
annotation_move.input_or_base_case_marked: Input cells or base case marked
annotation_move.shared_scale_across_panels: Shared scale or order held across panels (a corpus coders' term with no row of its own)
annotation_move.reading_key: Reading key or how-to-read note (a corpus coders' term with no row of its own)

emphasis_device.bold_or_coloured_lead_in: Bold or coloured lead-in or key phrase
emphasis_device.single_emphasis_colour: Single emphasis colour on one item
emphasis_device.shaded_key_rows: Shaded key rows, cells or columns
emphasis_device.dark_label_cells_or_banners: Navy or dark label cells or banners
emphasis_device.arrow_connectors: Arrows, chevrons or wedges as connectors

number_format.units_in_header: Units in a column or axis header
number_format.currency_first_and_total_rows: $ only on the first and total rows
number_format.nm_na_written: NM and NA written out, never blank

legend.direct_labels: Series named on the marks (end or direct labels)
legend.swatch_text: Swatches with text in the series colour
legend.none_needed: One series, or no series: nothing to name

colour_logic.single_hue_plus_highlight: Tints of one hue plus one "look here" colour
colour_logic.single_hue: Tints of one hue, no highlight
colour_logic.semantic: Colour carries sign, status or heat

corpus_spelling.about: How the corpus taxonomy spells the same terms. The corpus starter set is written in these spellings; library.py import reads them through this table and refuses a spelling not in it. Nothing else reads them: every tag is stored and checked as the slug.

annotation_move.inset_stats_table: inset stats table in the plot

annotation_move.shared_scale_across_panels: shared scale / order held across panels
